semantic_contract: The function copies a 12-byte three-dword resource key into a planet record's generated-terrain-key field, but only if the copy would change something. It compares the three incoming words against the three stored words in order and stops at the first difference; if all three match it returns without touching memory, and if any one differs it rewrites all three words unconditionally, so the write is all-or-nothing and never partial. It is void, has no callees, no branches beyond the compare chain, no frame, no saved registers and no side effects outside those three dwords. The receiver is not null-checked, so a null record faults. The paired getter 0x00b8dd60, ten lines below, treats a zero first word as 'nothing pending' and consumes the field once materialised, which is why writing a key that is already present is worth skipping. Of the sixteen observed callsites, thirteen write a computed key obtained from 0x00ba8010 and one (0x00c713c0) writes a key whose first word is the literal 0, i.e. deliberately clearing the field so the change check fires.
classification_rationale: Every element the vocabulary requires is read directly from the binary: the complete 17-instruction body, the __thiscall ABI with a proven callee-cleaned single stack dword, all three field offsets with the exact instructions that prove them, both branch polarities and the shared merge target, the absence of constants other than displacements, the absence of callees, globals and virtual dispatch, and the all-or-nothing write invariant. The field identity is not inferred from adjacency but corroborated four independent ways: the SDK declares the member at exactly 0x1A4 with a 0xC-byte ResourceKey type; the declared struct size 0x1B0 makes 0x1A4+0xC the exact end; the addressor 0x00b8d8e0 returns this+0x1A4; and the callers push the same property id 0x00B1B104 and offset 0x84 that the SDK's own GenerateTerrainKey uses. No material uncertainty remains in the reconstructed behaviour. The only thing not established is WHY the change check exists and which SDK method name, if any, corresponds to it, and those are naming and intent questions rather than behavioural ones, so they are recorded under unresolved_questions rather than used to lower the classification.
semantic_findings: The complete contract is `if (key != stored) { stored = key; }` over three dwords, void, no side effects.

The write is all-or-nothing. Both JNZ instructions target the same block at 0x00b8de04, and that block rewrites all three words regardless of which comparison failed. A partial write is not representable in this code.
The compare chain short-circuits: on a first-word difference the +0x04 and +0x08 loads and compares never execute.

The three field offsets 0x1A4, 0x1A8 and 0x1AC are consecutive and 0x1AC is the record's last word under the SDK's declared size 0x1B0, which is what makes the three comparisons a single 12-byte field rather than three unrelated ones.
The argument is a pointer, not a by-value key, so the caller retains ownership of the source and this function performs no copy of its own beyond the three MOVs.
A null receiver faults: the very first CMP dereferences ECX with no guard.

The field is a pending/lazy slot, not a plain cache. The paired getter 0x00b8dd60 treats a zero first word as an empty sentinel, asks a service to materialise the value, then zeroes the field, and reports failures with the hashed id 0x3D03F84 - a consume-once pattern.

Skipping an identical write is only observable if some consumer is watching the field. Since this function notifies nobody, the check most plausibly exists to keep an external watcher from seeing a redundant change; the paired getter is the only function found that both reads and clears the field, and it does notify 0x00b3d2a0's manager. Recorded as an inference, not a claim.

Sixteen callsites in thirteen functions, in two clusters: a 0x00BA* cluster that pushes the property descriptor 0x00B1B104 / 0x84 / 0xB0 before each call, and a 0x00BB2A50 cluster that repeats the pattern five times with different locals. Both clusters are property-binding plumbing, not gameplay logic.

The receiver is always reached indirectly - from a cStarRecord's planet vector at 0x00bbac80, from a +0x13C back-pointer at 0x00c713c0, or from a local/argument in the property binders - never as a global, so the record's lifetime is owned elsewhere and this function assumes it is alive.
unresolved_questions: Why does the change check exist? Nothing observable distinguishes skipping an identical write from performing it for a pure consumer, so the reason is unestablished. The most plausible purpose is suppressing a redundant change notification, but the notification for this setter's path was not found.

Which SDK method, if any, corresponds to this address? Spore-ModAPI declares `inline void cPlanetRecord::SetGeneratedTerrainKey(const ResourceKey& key) { mGeneratedTerrainKey = key; }` with no change check, so the name is explicitly withheld. The reconstructed name is descriptive and carries the VA token.
What is 0x00ba8010, the function that computes the key at nine of the sixteen callsites? Its body was not read by this batch, so the provenance of the written key is unestablished.
What does the +0x13C back-pointer at 0x00c713c0 point to, and why does that owner clear the key by writing a zero first word rather than calling a dedicated clear? Not established.

Is 0xB0 or 0xAF the correct fifth IDGenerator argument? cPlanetRecord.h:342 records 0xAF while the observed callsites push 0xB0. The property id 0x00B1B104 and the offset 0x84 match exactly, so the discrepancy is isolated to one argument of a related SDK function and does not affect any claim made here.

The briefing's canonical ledger recorded caller_count 12; the live xref query finds 16 call sites in 13 distinct caller functions. The four additional callers (0x00bbac80, 0x00c713c0, 0x00de6f20, 0x00f37690) are not a contradiction but a more complete count; 0x00bb2a50 alone accounts for five of the sixteen sites.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has ever been captured for this function; the original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run. Every claim here is static.

The change check is only observable through a watcher. A differential test must instrument the field or the paired getter to confirm that a redundant write really is suppressed, and to establish why the compiler emitted the check.

The consume-once behaviour of the paired getter 0x00b8dd60 is a runtime claim about the materialisation service obtained from 0x00f48a80; a write watchpoint on record+0x1A4 across a full planet load is required to confirm it.
No runtime evidence can distinguish 'write the same value' from 'skip the write' by observing memory alone, so any differential fixture for this function must observe side channels, not state.
